Data.SecondaryAudience: Lead Engineers, Security Architect, QA Lead

ToneOptions.Label: Authoritative & Precise
ToneOptions.FullPhrase: Maintain a highly authoritative and precise tone, focusing on technical accuracy and clarity.

ToneOptions.Label: Strategic & Visionary
ToneOptions.FullPhrase: Adopt a strategic and visionary tone, emphasizing future impact and architectural foresight.

ToneOptions.Label: Pragmatic & Actionable
ToneOptions.FullPhrase: Employ a pragmatic and actionable tone, guiding implementation with clear, concise instructions.

ToneOptions.Label: Security-Focused & Rigorous
ToneOptions.FullPhrase: Utilize a security-focused and rigorous tone, highlighting robust defense mechanisms and compliance.

GoalOptions.Label: Architectural Alignment
GoalOptions.Text: Ensure all stakeholders, especially Lead Engineers and the Security Architect, understand and align with the proposed event-driven architecture for the AI-Assisted Code Review & Security Gate. This document aims to secure consensus on the integration points and data flow within existing CI/CD pipelines, validating its fit within the enterprise's technical ecosystem.

GoalOptions.Label: Technical Feasibility
GoalOptions.Text: Demonstrate the technical feasibility and implementation strategy for the LLM-powered static analysis tool. The goal is to provide Lead Engineers with sufficient detail to begin planning development sprints, confirming that the solution can meet non-functional targets like low latency PR feedback and high accuracy in vulnerability detection.

GoalOptions.Label: Security & Compliance
GoalOptions.Text: Articulate the comprehensive security posture and compliance adherence of the AI-Assisted Code Review & Security Gate. This document seeks to reassure the Security Architect and QA Lead that the solution effectively mitigates OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities and integrates securely into the development lifecycle, meeting all relevant regulatory and internal security standards.

GoalOptions.Label: Performance & Scalability
GoalOptions.Text: Outline the performance characteristics and scalability strategy for the event-driven AI analysis system. The objective is to assure Lead Engineers and the Enterprise Architect that the solution can handle anticipated load, provide timely feedback for pull requests, and scale efficiently with increasing developer activity and code complexity without degrading service.

CriteriaOptions.Label: Technical & Operational Readiness
Criteria: All core event-driven components (e.g., message brokers, AI service endpoints) are clearly defined with their APIs and interaction patterns.
The document provides a detailed sequence diagram for the 'Developer opens PR -> AI analysis -> AI provides fix suggestions' flow, covering all primary actors.
Non-functional requirements for latency (e.g., PR feedback within X minutes) and accuracy (e.g., Y% detection rate for OWASP Top 10) are quantified and testable.
Integration points with existing SCM platforms (e.g., GitHub, GitLab) and CI/CD tools (e.g., Jenkins, Azure DevOps) are explicitly mapped and validated.

CriteriaOptions.Label: Security & Compliance Assurance
Criteria: The document explicitly addresses how the AI-Assisted Code Review & Security Gate detects and reports OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities.
Data privacy and security measures for code analysis (e.g., data anonymization, access controls for LLM interactions) are detailed.
Compliance with relevant industry standards (e.g., SOC 2, ISO 27001) regarding static analysis and security gates is outlined.
Mechanisms for auditing AI decisions and ensuring explainability for security findings are described.

CriteriaOptions.Label: Architectural & Strategic Alignment
Criteria: The proposed architecture for the AI-Assisted Code Review & Security Gate aligns with the enterprise's existing event-driven architecture principles.
The document clearly articulates the strategic benefits of the solution in terms of developer productivity and security posture improvement.
Potential architectural anti-patterns identified by the AI are categorized and mitigation strategies are proposed.
The long-term vision for evolving the AI capabilities (e.g., new detection types, custom rule sets) is presented.
